title: Prime Minister Modi Speaks To Nepal PM Balen Shah, Offers Full Humanitarian Assistance As 142 Indians Remain Missing After Flash Floods
text:
World
Swarajya Staff
Aug 27, 2026 | Updated 09:20 AM GMT+5:30

Prime Minister Narendra Modi spoke to his Nepalese counterpart Balendra Shah yesterday (26 August), offering full humanitarian assistance after devastating flash floods in Nepal left at least 160 people dead and hundreds missing.
Among those unaccounted for are 142 Indian nationals, many of whom were on pilgrimage to Mount Kailash in Tibet.
The catastrophic flooding struck Nepal's Rasuwa and Nuwakot districts on Wednesday (25 August) morning after an ice and rock avalanche triggered massive surges in the Bhote Koshi and Trishuli rivers.
Entire villages were swept away, along with roads, bridges and hydropower infrastructure. Authorities reported that 403 people remain missing, including 341 foreign nationals from India, the United States, Australia, the United Kingdom and other countries.
India is preparing to send emergency relief materials via Indian Air Force aircraft, including medicines, rations and essential supplies.
The government is also considering deploying National Disaster Response Force personnel to assist with rescue operations.
The Indian Embassy has established emergency helplines for affected nationals.
Climate experts at the International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development suggested the disaster was triggered by a glacier avalanche.
Nepali authorities have issued warnings for residents along the Bhote Koshi, Trishuli and Narayani rivers to remain vigilant.
Indian states Bihar and Uttar Pradesh have been placed on alert due to potential downstream flooding.
Nepal's tourism board clarified that the preliminary figures are being verified with travel agencies and local authorities.
Most missing Indian tourists were travelling through the Rasuwa region en route to the sacred Hindu site of Mount Kailash in Tibet.

The catastrophic flooding struck Nepal's Rasuwa and Nuwakot districts on Wednesday (25 August) morning after an ice and rock avalanche triggered massive surges in the Bhote Koshi and Trishuli rivers. India is preparing to send emergency relief materials via Indian Air Force aircraft, including medicines, rations and essential supplies.
